title: Small Cell Lung Cancer
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE Navigator (NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2026)
provenanceNote: Comprehensive NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2026 clinical navigator for Small Cell Lung Cancer (SCLC). Covers complete clinical algorithm: Diagnostic Workup (pathologic confirmation of small cell histology with neuroendocrine markers, contrast-enhanced CT chest/abdomen/pelvis, brain MRI with gadolinium, whole-body FDG-PET/CT for limited vs extensive stratification, baseline PFTs with performance status, laboratory evaluation with sodium and LDH) -> Stage Stratification (Limited-Stage LS-SCLC vs Extensive-Stage ES-SCLC vs Relapsed/Refractory platinum-resistant vs platinum-sensitive) -> LS-SCLC concurrent chemoradiation (platinum plus etoposide with early concurrent thoracic RT, PCI for responders, consolidative durvalumab maintenance per ADRIATIC) -> ES-SCLC first-line chemoimmunotherapy (platinum plus etoposide with atezolizumab per IMpower133 or durvalumab per CASPIAN, consolidative thoracic RT, MRI brain surveillance) -> Platinum-resistant relapse (lurbinectedin, topotecan, tarlatamab DLL3 BiTE per DeLLphi-301, palliative RT) -> Platinum-sensitive relapse (platinum doublet re-challenge, lurbinectedin, topotecan, or tarlatamab). References StewardMD Standard Protocols. DRAFT - clinical decision support; physician decides and dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
sourceNote: Structured in accordance with NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology (NCCN Guidelines) for Small Cell Lung Cancer Version 2.2026.

a.text: Brain MRI with and without gadolinium contrast is mandatory at diagnosis given the high incidence of brain metastases in SCLC; contrast-enhanced CT brain is used only when MRI is contraindicated.

b.text: Whole-body FDG-PET/CT from skull base to mid-thigh distinguishes limited-stage disease (confined to one hemithorax and regional nodes, encompassable in a single RT port) from extensive-stage disease (distant metastases, contralateral nodal disease, or malignant effusion).

c.text: LS-SCLC concurrent chemoradiation: cisplatin 60 mg/m2 day 1 (or carboplatin AUC 5-6) with etoposide 100 mg/m2 days 1-3 every 21 days for 4 cycles plus early concurrent thoracic RT (45 Gy in 1.5 Gy twice-daily fractions or 60-70 Gy once daily); PCI 25 Gy in 10 fractions for complete or partial responders; consolidative durvalumab maintenance for non-progressing patients per the ADRIATIC trial.

d.text: ES-SCLC first-line chemoimmunotherapy: carboplatin AUC 5 day 1 with etoposide 100 mg/m2 days 1-3 plus atezolizumab 1200 mg IV day 1 every 21 days for 4 cycles then atezolizumab 1200 mg every 3 weeks (IMpower133), or carboplatin AUC 5 / cisplatin 75-80 mg/m2 day 1 with etoposide 100 mg/m2 days 1-3 plus durvalumab 1500 mg IV day 1 every 21 days for 4 cycles then durvalumab 1500 mg every 4 weeks (CASPIAN). Consolidative thoracic RT for residual thoracic disease in responders; MRI brain surveillance is preferred over PCI.

e.text: Tarlatamab is a DLL3-targeted bispecific T-cell engager (BiTE) dosed 1 mg IV day 1, 10 mg day 8, 10 mg day 15, then 10 mg every 2 weeks per the DeLLphi-301 trial; monitor for cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS). Lurbinectedin 3.2 mg/m2 IV over 60 minutes every 21 days; topotecan 1.5 mg/m2/day IV days 1-5 every 21 days (or 2.3 mg/m2/day PO days 1-5).

nodes.name: Diagnostic Workup
nodes.title: Small Cell Lung Cancer: Diagnostic Workup Checklist
nodes.description: Step 1: Complete the clinical workup before stage stratification. Confirm small cell histology with neuroendocrine markers, stage the chest/abdomen/pelvis and brain, separate limited from extensive stage with PET/CT, and document pulmonary reserve and baseline laboratories.
bullets: Pathologic confirmation of small cell histology with neuroendocrine markers (synaptophysin, chromogranin, CD56, INSM1, Ki-67 >80-90%)
Contrast-enhanced CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis
Brain MRI with and without gadolinium contrast (mandatory due to high incidence of brain metastases; CT with contrast only if MRI contraindicated)
Whole-body FDG-PET/CT (skull base to mid-thigh) to differentiate limited from extensive stage
Baseline pulmonary function testing (PFTs: FEV1, DLCO) and performance status evaluation prior to concurrent chemoradiation
Laboratory evaluation: CBC, CMP, sodium (screening for SIADH), LDH, and liver function tests

nodes.name: Stage Stratification
nodes.title: Small Cell Lung Cancer: Stage Stratification
nodes.description: Workup complete. Assign limited vs extensive stage from anatomic extent and RT-port encompassability, or classify relapse by interval from completion of first-line platinum; the group selects the concurrent chemoradiation, chemoimmunotherapy, or relapsed-therapy pathway.
nodes.path: Small Cell Lung Cancer / Stage Stratification
bullets: Limited-Stage SCLC (LS-SCLC): disease confined to one hemithorax with regional nodes, tolerable in a single radiation port.
Extensive-Stage SCLC (ES-SCLC): distant metastases, contralateral nodal disease, or malignant effusion.
Relapsed / Refractory platinum-resistant SCLC: relapse less than 6 months from completion of first-line platinum.
Relapsed / Refractory platinum-sensitive SCLC: relapse 6 months or more from completion of first-line platinum.

nodes.name: Limited-Stage Treatment
nodes.title: LS-SCLC: Concurrent Chemoradiation Then PCI / Durvalumab Maintenance
nodes.description: Concurrent platinum-etoposide with early thoracic radiotherapy for limited-stage SCLC, followed by PCI for responders and consolidative durvalumab maintenance per ADRIATIC in non-progressing patients.
nodes.path: Small Cell Lung Cancer / Limited-Stage / Treatment
bullets: Concurrent Chemoradiation: Cisplatin 60 mg/m2 day 1 (or Carboplatin AUC 5-6) + Etoposide 100 mg/m2 days 1-3 every 21 days for 4 cycles with early concurrent Thoracic Radiotherapy (TRT: 45 Gy in 1.5 Gy twice-daily fractions or 60-70 Gy once daily).
Prophylactic Cranial Irradiation (PCI: 25 Gy in 10 fractions) for complete or partial responders after completion of concurrent chemoradiation.
Consolidative Durvalumab maintenance (ADRIATIC trial) after completion of concurrent chemoradiation in non-progressing patients.
Verify baseline PFTs (FEV1, DLCO) and performance status support concurrent chemoradiation before starting; monitor for esophagitis, pneumonitis, and myelosuppression during TRT.
Physician decides; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
nodes.regimenSummary: Cisplatin/Carboplatin + Etoposide + Early Concurrent TRT -> PCI / Durvalumab Maintenance (ADRIATIC)

nodes.name: Extensive-Stage Treatment
nodes.title: ES-SCLC: First-Line Chemoimmunotherapy Then IO Maintenance
nodes.description: First-line platinum-etoposide plus PD-L1 checkpoint inhibition (atezolizumab per IMpower133 or durvalumab per CASPIAN) for extensive-stage SCLC, with consolidative thoracic RT for residual disease and MRI brain surveillance.
nodes.path: Small Cell Lung Cancer / Extensive-Stage / Treatment
bullets: First-line Chemoimmunotherapy Option A: Carboplatin AUC 5 day 1 + Etoposide 100 mg/m2 days 1-3 + Atezolizumab 1200 mg IV day 1 every 21 days for 4 cycles, then Atezolizumab maintenance 1200 mg every 3 weeks (IMpower133 trial).

First-line Chemoimmunotherapy Option B: Carboplatin AUC 5 or Cisplatin 75-80 mg/m2 day 1 + Etoposide 100 mg/m2 days 1-3 + Durvalumab 1500 mg IV day 1 every 21 days for 4 cycles, then Durvalumab maintenance 1500 mg every 4 weeks (CASPIAN trial).
Consolidative thoracic RT for residual thoracic disease in responding patients.
MRI brain surveillance preferred over PCI in responding extensive-stage patients.
Physician decides; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
nodes.regimenSummary: Platinum + Etoposide + Atezolizumab or Durvalumab x 4 cycles -> IO Maintenance

nodes.name: Platinum-Resistant Relapse Treatment
nodes.title: Platinum-Resistant Relapse: Lurbinectedin, Topotecan, or Tarlatamab
nodes.description: Second-line and subsequent therapy for platinum-resistant or refractory relapse (relapse less than 6 months from first-line platinum): lurbinectedin, topotecan, or tarlatamab DLL3 BiTE with palliative RT for brain or bone metastases.
nodes.path: Small Cell Lung Cancer / Relapsed Refractory Platinum-Resistant / Treatment
bullets: Lurbinectedin 3.2 mg/m2 IV infusion over 60 minutes every 21 days.
Topotecan 1.5 mg/m2/day IV days 1-5 every 21 days (or 2.3 mg/m2/day PO days 1-5).
Tarlatamab (DLL3-targeted bispecific T-cell engager / BiTE, DeLLphi-301 trial: 1 mg IV day 1, 10 mg day 8, 10 mg day 15, then 10 mg every 2 weeks; monitor for CRS and ICANS).
Palliative radiotherapy for brain or bone metastases.
Physician decides; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
nodes.regimenSummary: Lurbinectedin 3.2 mg/m2 or Topotecan or Tarlatamab (DLL3 BiTE) 10 mg q2w

nodes.name: Platinum-Sensitive Relapse Treatment
nodes.title: Platinum-Sensitive Relapse: Platinum Re-challenge, Lurbinectedin, or Tarlatamab
nodes.description: Therapy for platinum-sensitive relapse (6 months or more from first-line platinum): retreatment with the original platinum doublet, or lurbinectedin, topotecan, or tarlatamab DLL3 BiTE.
nodes.path: Small Cell Lung Cancer / Relapsed Refractory Platinum-Sensitive / Treatment
bullets: Retreatment with original first-line platinum doublet (Carboplatin or Cisplatin + Etoposide) for platinum-sensitive relapse (6 months or more from completion of first-line platinum).
Lurbinectedin 3.2 mg/m2 IV every 21 days as an alternative systemic option.
Topotecan (1.5 mg/m2/day IV days 1-5 every 21 days or 2.3 mg/m2/day PO days 1-5) as an alternative systemic option.
Tarlatamab (DLL3 BiTE) 10 mg every 2 weeks as an alternative systemic option with CRS and ICANS monitoring.
Physician decides; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
nodes.regimenSummary: Platinum + Etoposide Re-challenge or Lurbinectedin or Tarlatamab DLL3 BiTE
